doc.title: Paquito D'Rivera — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Boy wonder of the saxophone on TV and with orchestras
summary: As a child prodigy he did TV shows from about age six, recitals and played transcribed Artie Shaw and Benny Goodman solos with orchestras.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Now before that, I understand that at age 10, you made your first performance with the national theater orchestra.
Yea, well I used to go around, I became what you call, uh,uh, a show boat. You know—

Yea. So, I made jokes, I play the saxophone in the store, I would play different kinds of music, and beside that I give some recitals of classical music. It was a combination of both. I used to do TV shows.
Seven. Eight. Even I think the first time I did a TV show, I was like six.
So, you were like the Boy Wonder of the saxophone.
Ah, something like that. [Both laugh] And I used to copy solos by Artie Shaw or Benny Goodman and play a solo, and take the Bennie Goodman or Artie Shaw orchestration, then I play
with the orchestra, I play the entire solo, and I improvise solo, I transcribe it, by ear. I used to do that.
